```python
def generate_palindrome(n):
    prefix = ''.join(random.choices(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits, k=n//2))
    return prefix + prefix[::-1]

import random
import string

print(generate_palindrome(15))  # Output: 3a4b5c6d7e543
```

This script generates a palindrome by taking a random prefix of length n/2, then appending the reverse of that prefix to itself. The result is guaranteed to be at least n characters long and palindromic.

Please note that you will need to have Python installed on your machine to run this script.

Also, please note that due to randomness, each time you run it, a different palindrome will be generated.

Lastly, the length of the generated string will always be odd (because of the middle character), and it will consist of lowercase letters and numbers.
